Senior DevOps Engineer (Security and Reliability)

Physitrack PLC · Fully remote, based in Poland Contract: B2B contractor, EUR 8,000 per month

About us

Physitrack PLC builds digital health software used by clinicians, physiotherapists and employers in over 100 countries. Our two product lines, Physitrack (exercise prescription, telehealth and patient engagement) and Champion Health (workplace wellbeing), run on a multi-region AWS platform serving Europe, the UK, North America, Australia and the Middle East.

We are ISO 27001:2022 certified. We hold clinical data and a large proprietary content library, and both need defending properly.

The role

You will own the security and reliability surface of our infrastructure: the edge, the data layer, and the observability stack that tells us when either is misbehaving. It sits where security engineering meets SRE. You will design controls at the edge, harden our cloud posture, make sure we can see what is happening across a multi-region estate, then evidence all of it to auditors and enterprise customers. This is hands-on engineering, not a governance role.

We are recruiting two senior infrastructure roles. This one covers the edge, observability and cloud security posture. The other, Senior DevOps Engineer (Platform), covers the Kubernetes estate, delivery pipelines and migrations. Apply for whichever fits, and tell us if both do.

What you will do

Edge and network security

  • Own our Envoy based edge, along with WAF rules, rate limiting and bot management across our cloud and CDN layers

  • Design and tune protections against abuse, including content scraping, credential attacks and traffic anomalies

  • Build detection for the traffic patterns that matter, and keep improving its signal to noise ratio

Cloud security posture

  • Harden our AWS estate: IAM boundaries, least privilege access, threat detection and runtime monitoring on EKS

  • Manage secrets, certificates and token lifecycle across the platform

  • Produce the infrastructure evidence behind ISO 27001 audits, penetration tests and enterprise security reviews

Data platform

  • Run PostgreSQL and RDS in production across regions, covering upgrades, performance, encryption and access control

  • Own our search infrastructure, Typesense and vector search, end to end

  • Work with MongoDB and Elasticache alongside the primary data stores

Observability

  • Own the monitoring platform: Grafana, Loki and Prometheus, plus Sentry and PagerDuty

  • Build alerting people actually trust, with meaningful thresholds, low noise and clear runbooks

  • Improve how logs and metrics flow from the edge and the application into the stack

What we are looking for

Essential

  • 5+ years in infrastructure, SRE or security engineering, with strong AWS depth

  • Real experience with edge, WAF or reverse proxy technology: Envoy, nginx, Cloudflare, ModSecurity, Coraza or equivalent

  • Production Kubernetes, ideally EKS, and strong Terraform

  • Operating PostgreSQL at scale. You have done upgrades and performance work, not just connected to one

  • Practical observability experience. You have built alerting that worked, and killed alerting that did not

  • A security engineer's instincts. You think about what an attacker does with the thing you just shipped

  • English at a working professional level. Our engineering team is international

Nice to have

  • Search infrastructure: Typesense, Elasticsearch, OpenSearch or vector search

  • Content protection and anti-scraping work

  • Having supported ISO 27001, SOC 2 or similar audits from the technical side

  • Healthcare, fintech or another regulated domain

  • Polish. Much of the engineering team is in Poland, though the company works in English

How we work

  • On-call. We run a 24/7 rotation through PagerDuty, with documented playbooks and readiness checklists. Participation is agreed with you rather than assumed, and separately compensated.

  • Cadence. Written async updates, a fortnightly planning touchpoint and a regular infrastructure and security sync. You set your own hours and choose your own tools.

  • Documentation. Threat models, decision records and runbooks are part of the work. We expect the reasoning to be written down, not just the config.

  • Autonomy. Small team, wide scope, very little process between you and a decision.

jobs.description:
About GBG

Enabling safe and rewarding digital lives for genuine people, everywhere

We make it our mission to ensure more genuine people have digital access to opportunities, and businesses have access to more genuine people. Our technology draws on diverse and reliable data to create a single point of truth for identity and address verification.

With over 30 years of experience behind us our team and technology are focused on enabling safe and rewarding digital lives for everyone. Regardless of age, location or background, genuine people everywhere should be able to digitally prove who they are and where they live.

About the team and role

GBG Go is the platform our customers use to design, deploy and operate identity verification journeys. It is where our data, decisioning and orchestration capabilities are exposed to the world — through the Go API, through Hosted Journeys that customers embed directly into their own onboarding flows, and through the Interactions Editor that lets them configure and evolve those journeys without writing code.

We are looking for a Senior Engineering Manager to lead the Go Core Platform group: three full-stack squads, each aligned to one of these value streams. You will be accountable for the health, throughput and technical direction of all three, and for the coherence of the platform they collectively build — a single product experience rather than three adjacent ones.

This is a hands-on leadership role for someone who is as comfortable in an architecture discussion as in a performance conversation. You will report into the SVP of Product Engineering and work closely with Product, Design, Architecture and Customer-facing teams.

Alongside delivery, you will play a leading role in maturing how we build. GBG is investing in AI-enabled engineering, and this group is one of the places where that practice gets proven before it scales. You will shape the standards, guardrails and measurement that turn AI from individual experimentation into dependable organisational capability.

What you will do

Delivery Leadership Across Three Value Streams

  • Own delivery outcomes for the Go API, Hosted Journeys and Interactions Editor squads — scope, sequencing, quality and predictability
  • Create clear commitments with Product and hold the line on them, while being honest early when reality changes
  • Keep the three streams moving independently where they can and coordinated where they must, managing cross-squad dependencies before they become blockers
  • Establish and use meaningful delivery signals (flow, cycle time, change failure rate, escaped defects) to drive decisions rather than to report activity

Technical Direction and Platform Coherence

  • Partner with architects and senior engineers on the technical direction of the Go core: API design and versioning, journey runtime behaviour, configuration modelling, and the boundaries between them
  • Hold the group to a shared standard for reliability, performance, observability and security of customer-facing surfaces
  • Actively manage technical debt and platform resilience as a planned investment, not a residual activity
  • Make sure the three streams converge on shared patterns, components and contracts instead of drifting into three dialects of the same platform

AI-Enabled Engineering and SDLC Maturity

  • Lead adoption of AI-assisted development across your squads — coding agents, review assistance, test generation, documentation and beyond
  • Define what good looks like: prompting and context practices, human review expectations, evaluation of generated output, and the guardrails that keep quality and security non-negotiable
  • Establish measurement for adoption and impact — on throughput, quality, and developer experience — and be rigorous about distinguishing real gains from perceived ones
  • Codify what works into repeatable practice and share it outward, contributing to standards and enablement across the wider engineering organisation
  • Adapt planning, estimation and review rituals to a world where the constraint is increasingly judgement and verification rather than authoring speed

People Leadership

  • Lead, coach and grow full-stack engineers across three squads, including tech leads and senior individual contributors
  • Set clear expectations, give direct and useful feedback, and run a fair, evidence-based approach to performance and progression
  • Own hiring for the group, and raise the bar on how we assess engineers as you go
  • Build squads that are engaged and psychologically safe, and that take genuine ownership of what they run in production
  • Stakeholder Partnership and Communication
  • Act as the engineering counterpart to Product leadership for the Go core roadmap
  • Translate technical reality into terms commercial and executive stakeholders can act on — trade-offs, risks and confidence levels, not jargon
  • Represent the group in incident, escalation and customer-critical situations, and lead the follow-through afterwards

Skills we're looking for

  • Significant engineering management experience, including leading multiple teams or a group of squads (ideally 20+ engineers, directly and through tech leads)
  • Track record delivering and operating customer-facing SaaS platforms at scale — public APIs, embedded/hosted experiences, or configuration-driven products
  • Credible full-stack technical depth: enough to challenge design decisions on both the service and front-end side, without needing to make them yourself
  • Strong grasp of modern engineering practice — CI/CD, trunk-based development, feature flagging, progressive delivery, testing strategy, observability
  • Demonstrable, practical experience with AI-assisted development workflows, and a clear point of view on where they help, where they don't, and how to tell the difference
  • Comfort with metrics and systems thinking — able to build measurement that changes behaviour rather than just populates a dashboard
  • Ability to lead in a globally distributed environment, and to influence peers and squads you don't directly own
  • Excellent communication across technical, product and executive audiences
  • Nice to Have
  • Experience in identity verification, fraud, KYC/AML, RegTech or another regulated data domain
  • Background with journey orchestration, workflow engines, low-code configuration tooling, or embeddable SDKs and widgets
  • Experience building or scaling internal developer platforms and enablement practice

Remote — Data Insights Team — Full-time

Modash gives brands the tools to work with the right content creators and helps creators earn a living doing what they love. Behind the scenes, the Data Insights team is building the intelligence layer that turns raw social media signals into trusted, customer-facing data products — with reliable access, quality, and freshness at scale.⁠

We’re looking for a hardened Senior Product Data Engineer to help us scale these systems end-to-end, raise our quality bar, and accelerate how quickly we turn messy public data into consistent, valuable insights customers can build on.⁠⁠⁠​

🚀 What your day-to-day will look like

We’re not a service function — Data Search & Data Insights are core product capabilities at Modash, building products for customers to use. Data Insights is a specialised team in Data Org, and you’ll own high impact projects end-to-end, from idea to launch.

Here’s a typical day:

  • Start your day with a short standup
  • Heads-down focus time to plan, build, iterate, and launch
  • Minimal meetings — maximum ownership

You’ll be working on big, impactful projects like:

  • Creating an understanding of the creators location, age, and interests at scale
  • Creating systems to extract collaborations between creators and brands from raw social data
  • Shaping the future of AI-assisted search, exploring how LLMs and embeddings can enhance search and recommendations.

You won’t be patching pipelines — you’ll be creating data products from scratch that directly impact customers.

👥 The Data Team

At Modash, the Data Insights team isn’t a support function — it’s a core part of the product. You’ll join a growing group of data and backend engineers, working within our broader Data organization.

We work in three closely aligned teams within Data:

  • Data Insights — builds the creator and brand-level insight products and APIs (e.g., collaborations, reports, dictionaries, contacts, audience overlap).
  • Data Search — owns our search products (including AI Search) end-to-end.
  • Data Core — responsible for raw data collection and the foundations of our data platform.

We value autonomy, but we also work closely as a team — through pair programming, fast feedback loops, and shared wins. Everyone is expected to take ownership, but nobody works in isolation.

We’re remote-first, and we also make time to connect IRL through regular team offsites — to have fun, collaborate, and reflect.

⚙️ Our tech stack

  • AWS and GCP with Pulumi (IaC)
  • PySpark on AWS EMR for compute
  • GCP Vertex Batch API for LLMs
  • Airflow for orchestration
  • Iceberg and Aurora (Postgres) for persistence
  • Other: S3, Glue, Kinesis, Lambda, ECS, Athena
  • Tools: Slack, GitHub, Linear, Notion, Cursor

🧪 The interview process

We move fast. You can get interviewed in under a week. Process consists of:

1. Intro chat

2. Technical interviews: 1. Coding challenge (in PySpark) and 2. System Design

3. Team fit / Project presentation

4. Culture & alignment call with the CEO Avery Schrader - That’s it!

Requirements

🛠 Skillset we’re looking for

  • Strong knowledge of Spark (Scala, Databricks, or PySpark; PySpark preferred but not required)
  • Proven track record with ETL/ELT pipelines and large-scale data processing
  • Comfortable working with unstructured data
  • Experience with workflow orchestration tools like Airflow or AWS Step Functions
  • Familiarity with the AWS ecosystem (Glue, EMR, etc.)
  • You've shipped full features from idea to production: planning & scoping → architecture → implementation → release → iteration
  • Based in Europe with significant working-hours overlap with EET (Tallinn time)
  • Hands-on experience building agentic / LLM-powered features in production
  • Practical understanding of trade-offs between LLMs (cost, latency, capability)

✅ Bonus points if you…

  • Have worked with AI/ML tools or LLMs
  • Are familiar with the GCP stack (especially Vertex AI)
  • Have worked with lakehouse formats like Apache Iceberg
  • Have used Pulumi or Terraform for IaC
  • Are familiar with Node.js and TypeScript
  • Understand AWS cost mechanics (how scale impacts spend)
  • Care deeply about code quality and system design
  • Are curious about the creator economy (we'll help you get up to speed)

Not a fit if...

  • Your data engineering experience is primarily in analytics or BI (dashboards, internal reporting, warehouse modeling for analysts)
  • You haven't built and operated data products that ship as part of a customer-facing application
  • You're looking for a role focused on stakeholder reporting rather than building production data systems

🧑‍🔧 We’re looking for people that

  • Are tirelessly in search of the best versions of ourselves – Who want to really show what they’ve got and want to prove the world and themselves what they’re capable of.
  • Are direct in their communication – We support and encourage one another through direct, immediate & helpful feedback.
  • Know how to become autonomous - Who we can trust to do their best work without needing processes to guardrail.
  • Are willing to take ownership to stand up for ourselves, our teams, and our communities.
  • Have fun, are honest, and do great work – No title chasers, no finger pointers, no being awful. Absolutely no slowing down to protect ego.

Benefits

🎁 What we offer

  • Fully remote — work from anywhere in Europe
  • Compensation. Your compensation is made up of salary and stock options. As we're growing fast, the stock option package is especially significant. Annual salary range is 90,000€ - 140,000€ for this role. We hire across Europe, so the exact number depends on your location, employment type, skills, and experience.
  • Unlimited paid vacation 🌴
  • Flexible hours — async-friendly culture
    High ownership, low bureaucracy, no bullshit.
  • Personal development support — courses, books, or conferences on us
  • Regular offsites — connect with your team IRL

Help us build the data backbone of the creator economy. Apply now — we’d love to meet you.😊

And a little more about us...

Founded by a high-school dropout and a Canadian (yes, we’re also shocked it’s going so well), Modash is building a suite of tools that help brands scale partnerships with online content creators.

1500+ companies like Google, Wolt (Doordash), Bolt, and Nord VPN, Stanley and others use Modash to find, analyze and monitor social media creators.

We have some very big customers. Some have already changed the world. But many of them are just starting out. Modash is their first customer acquisition channel and we help make their missions come to life, in our small way.

We’re a profitable company. We’re also backed by the best investors in Europe. Including Icebreaker.vc, Change Ventures, and a group of Europe’s top founders.

We’re a small team and we’re just getting started. You’ll work with people who have done everything from building solar cars to hanging out with Metallica and Bon Jovi.

Folks who have seen the inner workings of companies like Amazon, Veriff, Pipedrive, Yes, and the burning man of startups - Pirate summit. Come be great and do great things and make great stuff and create great memories while making a great impact. Do it.

Meet your future colleagues!

Accountability

Content Strategy & Editorial Direction

Community Management & Engagement

  • Exercise strong judgment when responding to sensitive health conversations.
  • Escalate clinical or high-risk questions where appropriate rather than providing unsupported medical guidance.

Content Accuracy & Approval

  • Coordinate with relevant internal stakeholders to ensure health-related content is reviewed before publication.
  • Establish a lightweight and dependable approval process.
  • Balance accuracy with the need to maintain content velocity.
  • Ensure claims and educational content are appropriately validated.

jobs.title: Health Coach (Dietitian/Nutritionist) - Specialist Weight Management, Remote
jobs.excerpt: Full-Time | Fully Remote | Some Evening and Weekend Working Required | Fixed-Term Contract We're looking for an HCPC-registered Dietitian or AfN-registered Nutritionist to join our growing clinical team at one of the UK's most exciting health-tech companies.
jobs.description:
Full-Time | Fully Remote | Some Evening and Weekend Working Required | Fixed-Term Contract

We're looking for an HCPC-registered Dietitian or AfN-registered Nutritionist to join our growing clinical team at one of the UK's most exciting health-tech companies.

In this role, you'll support people living with obesity to make sustainable lifestyle and behaviour changes, working as part of a multidisciplinary team within our Specialist Weight Management Service (SWMS).

This is a fully remote role: all delivery is via video consultation and in-app messaging, and you can be based anywhere in the UK. Flexibility is required to support some early evenings and Saturdays as and when needed to support our NHS contracts.

The Challenge

More than 1 in 4 adults in the UK are living with obesity; a chronic condition that often negatively impacts their physical and mental health, and therefore quality of life. Access to specialist weight management services for the treatment of obesity remains limited and varies geographically due to a lack of funding. Existing services face long waiting lists, resulting in treatment delays which can adversely affect patient outcomes.

Enter Second Nature...

By bringing together the latest behavioural science, psychology, technology, and the talents of our incredible team, our mission is to eradicate obesity and type 2 diabetes for all, and as part of that mission, we are aiming to increase access to effective treatment for people living with obesity. Second Nature provides specialist weight management services to support people living with obesity.

About us:

  • We've positively changed the lives of 300,000+ people through accessible, evidence-based healthcare.
  • We're rated 'Excellent' on Trustpilot by over 8,000 of our members.
  • We're the UK’s largest digital health provider to the NHS
  • We're a leading B2C provider of GLP-1 medication-assisted weight loss programmes, and 1 of 5 NICE-approved providers to deliver these services within the NHS in the future
  • Our team members stay with us for an average of 4.3 years

The Role

We're looking for a dynamic Health Coach who is passionate about making a positive difference to those living with obesity to grow our current clinical team. You will be part of an innovative Specialist Weight Management Service (SWMS) that uses a multi-disciplinary team (MDT) approach to obesity treatment and technology to optimise patient engagement and outcomes. Our MDT includes doctors, dietitians, psychologists and physical activity specialists, all with special interests in obesity.

You will provide nutritional and lifestyle interventions to people living with obesity to support them to make sustainable dietary and behaviour changes, in collaboration with the MDT. You'll be using evidence-based health coaching techniques, such as motivational interviewing, goal setting and behaviour change frameworks. Whilst it is important to be able to work autonomously, you will receive comprehensive training. You will also have access to clinical supervision and support from senior clinicians.

This post is full-time (40 hours/week) and fixed-term, with flexible hours and a view to extend based on the needs of the service. You'll work fully remotely, connecting with service users through video consultations and in-app messaging. The role requires working some early evenings per week and Saturdays as and when needed to support our NHS contracts.

What you'll do:

  • Independently implement appropriate initial assessment methods to allocate service users to the most suitable treatment pathway
  • Deliver group-based and one-to-one nutritional and lifestyle interventions remotely via video calls, to support changes in dietary and physical activity behaviours
  • Provide ongoing coaching and support between sessions through in-app messaging
  • Support service users across both medicated and non-medicated programmes, including those accessing GLP-1 medication
  • Attend regular MDT meetings to monitor the care of our service users
  • Attend clinical supervision to discuss complex or high-risk cases
  • Appropriately manage clinical risk (e.g. safeguarding concerns) when it arises during clinical practice
  • Maintain adequate CPD, receive regular clinical supervision in accordance with good practice guidelines and continue to meet your registration requirements (HCPC or AfN)
  • Maintain confidentiality of information in line with the requirements of the Data Protection Act and ensuring that participant confidentiality is protected at all times
  • Contribute to innovation projects, service evaluation, and ongoing programme development at Second Nature

Requirements

You have experience working in a weight management/bariatric/eating disorder setting

  • A qualified HCPC-registered Dietitian or AfN-registered Nutritionist with experience of weight management and/or bariatric experience, or working with patients in an eating disorder setting
  • Proven experience delivering group-based programmes, with the confidence to facilitate sessions effectively in a digital setting
  • A solid understanding of obesity as a condition and the issues many people living with obesity face, including weight stigma
  • Experience or training in health coaching, behaviour change, or motivational interviewing, with awareness of coaching models and approaches
  • Able to provide supportive, empathetic patient-centred care to patients who may have complex physical and mental health needs

You're comfortable working fully remotely

  • You enjoy remote working and can stay motivated and organised without an office around you
  • You have a suitable home working setup, including a private space for confidential consultations and a reliable internet connection

You can work autonomously and collaboratively with a doctor-led multidisciplinary team (MDT) to oversee patient care

  • You'll confidently and independently manage a caseload of service users, delivering nutritional and lifestyle interventions via video calls and in-app messaging, and working collaboratively with our MDT

You have experience in supporting the coordination of a healthcare service

  • You have experience in monitoring and supporting patients' journeys through a service in line with an organisation's protocols, including scheduling assessments and appointments, monitoring attendance rates and following up with patients, writing GP letters, and revising protocols
  • You have experience using Excel or Google Sheets (or other similar programmes) to monitor patients' journeys

You are dynamic and have a strong drive to work in healthcare tech

  • You have experience thriving in fast-paced environments and are energised by the dynamic nature of start-up life, where being hands-on and adaptable to the evolving needs of the service is essential
  • You're confident in using technology to provide patient care, including recording and reviewing patient notes, and providing in-app coaching
  • Excited by digital initiatives that increase access to healthcare

Education/Qualifications:

  • HCPC registration as a Dietitian, or AfN registration as a Nutritionist (Registered Nutritionist or Registered Associate Nutritionist)
  • Relevant degree in Dietetics, Nutrition or a related field

To apply

Please submit your CV and cover letter via this application page, and include your HCPC or AfN registration number. Unfortunately, we're unable to progress applications without appropriate registration. Due to the high volume of applications we receive, we may not be able to respond to everyone individually. If we don't have a chance to get back to you, we're not intentionally being rude, but please assume it's a no for now!

Benefits

  • Work from home with flexible hours
  • Joining a culture of intelligent, friendly, and highly-motivated individuals who are passionate about what they do
  • A competitive market salary
  • 25 days of holiday plus national holidays

jobs.title: Freelance Finance Content Writer
jobs.excerpt: Please note: We're receiving a high volume of applications and it may be some time before your application is reviewed.
jobs.description:
Please note: We're receiving a high volume of applications and it may be some time before your application is reviewed.

Are you aching to write content that brings in real results and that people actually read rather than another generic piece of content?

Are you obsessed with understanding how a product works and how to make it appealing to a reader?

Do you continuously look for ways to improve your writing, and dream of becoming a writer who can confidently say their content brings in customers?

Then read on… this freelance position may be right for you!

*Please note: we aren't accepting candidates who are in full-time employment

About the position

Mint Studios is a content marketing agency based in the UK and US that helps financial services companies like Modulr, Zai, Confused.com and Jeeves acquire customers with content. We use our four pillar framework to help financial services companies turn their blog into a customer acquisition channel:

  1. A content strategy based on customer research and focused on Bottom of the Funnel keywords
  2. Content written for the level of the reader and focused on the company's product
  3. Content based on interviews with subject matter experts
  4. Content results that can be tracked

We’re currently looking for writers to work with us. If you’re interested, here’s more information on what we’re looking for.

Responsibilities

  • Write 3 - 4 articles per month for one client
  • Each article is usually 2,000 - 3,000 words, and takes around 2 weeks to write in between rounds of edits
  • 90% of articles are based on a recording of an interview with a subject matter expert combined with desk research
  • The process includes one outline, then 2 rounds of edits
  • Edit content based on feedback
  • Complete a comprehensive questionnaire and outline (our version of the “brief”) before writing the first draft.
  • Acquire knowledge about our clients, their products or services and the audience we’re targeting (you don’t need a background in fintech or financial services!)

What we're looking for

You don’t have to have a background in fintech or financial services – we can teach you that. What we really value is attitude and good writing.

These are the 7 characteristics of the best writers that we work with at Mint Studios:

  1. You have clarity of thought. You can put together logical arguments in the written form and when you don’t understand something you’ll take the time to understand it.
  2. You are inherently curious. You want to understand a topic inside out. You’ll do the right amount of research and ask the right questions till you feel confident writing and talking about the topic.
  3. You are detail oriented. You care about delivering something great, even when no one is watching.
  4. You’re constantly thinking of the bigger picture. You like to understand how the content in the interview fits into the product, the client, and the strategy.
  5. You take responsibility for your skillset. You’re always trying to become a better writer and are open to new processes and ways of working.
  6. You are empathetic. You can put yourself in the shoes of the reader and of the client. You try to understand their perspective and will ask questions if you don’t.
  7. You like working with smart, fun and collaborative people where you are supported and your career is developed!

You might not be a good fit if...

  • You don't enjoy explaining complex topics.
  • You are a creature of habit and prefer to stick to your own writing processes or are not open to learning new processes.
  • You don't enjoy the research process (understanding the topic, product and the content strategy in depth, listening to and analysing the interview for the main takeaways, etc).
  • You don't like asking for advice, asking questions or you are not comfortable with feedback.
  • You are not interested in improving your writing skills

The password to apply is: The Hobbit

About Mint Studios

Mint Studios is a content marketing agency that helps helps financial services companies acquire customers and position themselves as experts with content marketing.

Our main differentiation point from other agencies is that we create content that is optimised for conversions and leads, not just traffic. We do this by creating Bottom of the Funnel content, which involves understanding our client’s ideal customer and creating content that is designed to sell, not entertain. You can learn more about BOFU here: What is BOFU (Bottom of the Funnel) Content and Why Is it Important?

Although we only work with financial services companies, these range from crypto, to budgeting apps, to enterprise payments companies and consultancies. You won’t be writing about the same topics over and over again.

These are some examples of BOFU content we’ve written for clients:

  • How To Get Health Insurance As An Expat In The Philippines
  • Paying International Vendors & Suppliers: What’s the Best Way?
  • Wave Alternative In Australia: Parpera
  • Top corporate incubators [2023]

Examples of more technical content:

  • Top marketplace payment providers in Australia: We compare 4!
  • Payroll payments solution: How to innovate with Modulr
  • Marketplace fraud prevention: how to fine-tune your current system

You can learn more about why we set up the agency here: Why I Set Out to Build a Financial Content Marketing Agency

  • Why I Joined Mint Studios: Michelle Maiellaro
  • Why I Joined Mint Studios: Elliot McGuire
  • Why I Joined Mint Studios: Katie Norris
  • Mint Studios Careers

Compensation and benefits of working with Mint Studios

  • We pay $300/£250/per article to begin with, and once you’re trained on our methodology and we’re confident in your writing (this usually takes 3 - 4 articles) we then go to the next stage, where we pay $450/£350 per article.
  • For our payment clients, we pay $600/£500 per article once you're trained.
  • If you pass our “probation period”, we can offer a long-term contract (at least 6 months). We can also offer a full-time position if you’re interested.
  • We pay on-time, usually on the first Friday of the month.
  • As long as articles are delivered on time, you can work when you want.
  • You don’t have to know about financial services (but you do have to be willing to learn). We value good writing more.
  • You’ll be able to see how your content delivers impact and helps our clients acquire customers.
  • We give a lot of detailed feedback. You won’t get vague feedback like “can you make this less confusing?”. We try to make our feedback to the point and we’ll always look for ways to improve the article ourselves (so you’re not left coming up with alternatives alone).
  • You’ll have the opportunity to grow: we only hire content strategists from within, and we’re always looking for strategists. You’ll have a chance of learning about content strategy and learning how to turn readers into leads.

Interested? Apply on the next page!

jobs.title: Event Production & Client Success Manager
jobs.excerpt: About From Day One:The business landscape is changing fast.
jobs.description:
About From Day One:

The business landscape is changing fast. From Day One is a media outlet and conference series that helps companies navigate all that change in ways that put people first.

Since our beginning in 2018, we've reached over 150,000 attendees, hosted over a thousand speakers, and produced conferences in more than 20 major U.S. cities–and counting. We take a unique, cross-disciplinary approach, convening leaders in CSR, HR, marketing, and communications, as well as civic leaders, authors, and journalists, to share business strategies that benefit workers, customers, and communities.

We also publish reporting and opinion pieces by a network of notable journalists, led by the company's editor in chief, veteran journalist Stephen Koepp.

At From Day One, we hire people who have a high degree of self-motivation and the potential to grow into active leaders. We call team members like these "drivers". If you are a passenger, From Day One will not be a good fit for you.

As you apply, think about whether these attributes describe you:

  • You motivate and energize colleagues rather than waiting for inspiration.
  • You're relentlessly resourceful and take ownership rather than seeking excuses. .
  • You look to consistently deliver great outcomes, and work to improve processes as you engage with them.
  • You are excited about your work and bring urgency to your mission.
  • You approach challenges with enthusiasm and optimism.

Our work is driven by our mission to improve the relationship between business and society, and our efforts are intended to contribute to a brighter future. By maintaining this optimistic outlook, we not only motivate ourselves but also uplift those around us. We believe that believing that the future will be better is the first step towards making it better -- for others, and for ourselves personally.

Please note that diversity and inclusion are absolutely core to our mission, and we are committed to those values in our hiring process.

About This Role:

The Event Production & Client Success Manager manages the logistical needs of our production calendar for both live and virtual events, and owns the relationships with the sponsors who attend them.

Production is the larger share of the job, and volume is what defines it. In the next twelve months we are producing thirteen live conferences and a virtual conference every month. Several events sit at different planning milestones at once, and you would carry them without being told what is due next.

Key tasks include managing A/V teams on visual and audio production needs, review and management of rental orders, vendor requirements and temporary staff hiring, creation of venue layouts and detailed run-of-show schedules, execution of vendor contracts, and construction of the event budget. Much of the work is reconciliation — the A/V order against the current slate of content, the final catering guarantee against the projection it came from, the printed program against the website and the run of show.

Alongside production you would be the point of contact for a roster of our sponsors, administering their deliverables and making sure their experience on site earns a renewal. Producing the event and serving the client are the same job here, done by the same person, which is what makes both halves work.

This is a remote position, and also includes regular travel to other cities for in-person events.

Responsibilities:

Event Production

  • Run the full production process for assigned conferences from the 180-day milestone through post-event wrap-up, and lead the milestone production meetings along the way
  • Create detailed run-of-show schedules and venue layouts, and manage room capacity against the final slate of content and expected attendance
  • Manage A/V teams on visual and audio production needs, walking the order line by line as content changes
  • Review and manage rental orders and vendor requirements, and hire and coordinate temporary event staff
  • Own vendor contracts across venue, catering, A/V, rentals, video, and photography, including deadlines and certificates of insurance
  • Manage catering selections and final guarantees, and compare final numbers against projections
  • Build and maintain the event budget from signed contracts and estimates, and track costs against it as scope changes
  • Place badge, program, and signage orders against their drop-dead dates, and coordinate shipping and staff travel
  • Produce our virtual events on platforms such as Zoom — setting up templates, managing schedules, and ensuring staffing of key roles

Client Success

  • Act as point of contact for a roster of sponsors on their event logistics, escalating as needed
  • Administer all sponsor deliverables — advance materials, shipping of display items, presentation media
  • Assign sponsor table locations, and confirm sponsor and speaker registrations against the production plan
  • Conduct post-event feedback calls, and contribute to renewal rate and customer satisfaction scores

Requirements

  • This position requires a 4-year college/university degree at minimum
  • Candidates should have a strong academic background and a minimum of 3 years of full-time, professional post-graduation experience
  • Direct experience producing complex events — corporate or marketing events, executive gatherings, conferences, trade shows, festivals, or arts events — where you were accountable for the event coming off
  • Experience as a named point of contact for external clients, sponsors, or partners

jobs.title: Senior Threat Engineer – AI-Powered Detection, Response & Continuous AI Red Team
jobs.excerpt: Job SummaryCatch attackers in minutes, not days.  Test our own defenses at attacker speed, continuously.
jobs.description:
Job Summary

Catch attackers in minutes, not days. Test our own defenses at attacker speed, continuously.

The Senior Threat Engineer is a hands‑on, high‑impact role within the Enterprise Defense & Automation (EDA) team. You will engineer AI‑powered detection and response capabilities that compress attacker dwell time from days to minutes, and you will continuously red team those same defenses at attacker speed so that gaps are found by us long before they are found by an adversary.

The role sits at the intersection of threat detection engineering, adversary emulation, and applied AI. On the defensive side you will build detections and AI‑assisted response paths that triage, decide, and act autonomously within policy, moving security operations from “alert and investigate” to detect, decide, and act. On the offensive side you will run continuous, automated adversary emulation against production controls, generating a constant stream of evidence about what our defenses actually stop.

This is a builder and problem‑solver role. You will write detection logic, adversary emulation content, and automated response playbooks; instrument them with measurable outcomes such as mean time to detect, mean time to contain, and detection coverage against MITRE ATT and use AI to raise signal fidelity rather than alert volume. Every detection you ship is expected to be tested by an emulation you also ship.

Success requires strong threat fundamentals, fluency across modern detection and response platforms, and the discipline to deliver production‑grade capability that holds up in real‑world, adversarial conditions. Guardrails matter as much as speed: confidence thresholds, blast‑radius limits, and rollback paths are part of the design, not an afterthought.

If you are energized by hunting real adversaries, teaching machines to respond faster than they can, and attacking your own work before anyone else gets the chance, this role puts you at the forefront of modern cyber defense.

What you will do

AI-Powered Detection & Response — catch attackers in minutes, not days (Primary)

  • Engineer high‑fidelity detections across identity, endpoint, network, cloud, and SaaS, and pair each one with an automated response path so the outcome is containment, not another alert.
  • Apply AI and machine learning to triage, correlate, and enrich alerts at machine speed — clustering related signals into a single incident narrative and surfacing the attacker story instead of a queue of fragments.
  • Build autonomous and semi‑autonomous response playbooks that isolate hosts, revoke sessions and tokens, disable credentials, block infrastructure, and quarantine content within minutes of first signal.
  • Implement the guardrails that make autonomy safe: confidence thresholds, blast‑radius controls, human‑in‑the‑loop escalation for high‑impact actions, and tested rollback for every automated action.
  • Instrument detection and response for measurable outcomes — mean time to detect, mean time to contain, false‑positive rate, and ATT&CK coverage — and drive those numbers down release over release.
  • Use LLMs and agentic tooling where they earn their place: summarizing investigations, drafting containment recommendations, extracting indicators from unstructured reporting, and generating detection logic that a human reviews before it ships.

Continuous AI Red Teaming — test our own defenses at attacker speed (Primary)

  • Stand up and operate continuous, automated adversary emulation against production controls, so defensive coverage is proven by evidence on a recurring cadence rather than assumed between annual assessments.
  • Use AI to generate and mutate attack behavior — varying tradecraft, tooling, and sequencing across ATT&CK techniques — so detections are tested against variants rather than a single static signature.
  • Close the loop from emulation to engineering: every miss becomes a detection backlog item, every noisy hit becomes a tuning task, and every fix is re‑tested automatically.
  • Red team our AI itself — test detection models, agents, and prompts for evasion, prompt injection, data poisoning, and unsafe autonomous action, and remediate what you find.
  • Operate emulation safely in production: scoped targets, rate limits, clear abort criteria, deconfliction with the response team, and full audit trails for every executed technique.
  • Report coverage as a living metric — which techniques are prevented, which are detected, which are only logged, and which are invisible — and use it to prioritize the detection roadmap.

Threat Research & Hunting

  • Track adversary tradecraft relevant to CDW and our customers, and translate intelligence into emulation plans, detections, and response actions rather than reading material.
  • Run hypothesis‑driven threat hunts across SIEM, XDR, identity, and cloud telemetry, and convert every confirmed hunt technique into an automated detection so the same hunt never has to be run by hand twice.
  • Map techniques to controls and automated responses once, then reuse the mapping globally across the estate.
  • Lead technical deep dives on significant incidents and emulation findings, and feed the lessons back into detection content, response playbooks, and platform hardening.

Detection Engineering as Code

  • Treat detection content as software: version controlled, peer reviewed, unit tested against emulation data and promoted through CI/CD with security gates that block low‑quality logic before it reaches production.
  • Develop integrations and tooling in Python against platform APIs and event‑driven architectures, favoring reusable services over one‑off scripts.
  • Build detection and response capability that self‑heals — identifying telemetry gaps, sensor degradation, and control drift, then correcting them or rolling back to a known‑good state without waiting for a human.
  • Eliminate repeat findings through native auto‑remediation patterns rather than recurring manual cleanup.

Collaboration & Influence

  • Partner closely with the Threat Response team, Cyber Defense Engineering, security platform owners, and business unit owners so that detections, emulations, and automated actions land with clear ownership boundaries.
  • Contribute to shared backlogs and design reviews, and mentor engineers and analysts on detection quality, adversary tradecraft, and the safe use of AI in the defensive stack.
  • Document detection logic, emulation plans, automation patterns, and engineering decisions so the capability survives any single person.

What we expect of you

  • Bachelor’s degree and 7+ years of experience in threat detection engineering, threat hunting, incident response, or offensive security, or 11+ years of equivalent experience.
  • Hands‑on experience building and tuning detections in SIEM platforms and cloud‑scale security tooling.
  • Practical working knowledge of the MITRE ATT&CK framework, including mapping detections and automated responses to techniques.
  • Experience with adversary emulation, purple teaming, breach and attack simulation, or penetration testing against production controls.
  • Proficiency in Python for production‑grade automation and tooling.
  • Experience applying AI/ML or LLM‑based capabilities to security problems, and designing secure, observable, and maintainable AI‑enabled solutions.
  • Working experience with security automation, orchestration, or SOAR platforms.
  • Built detection and response capability for large, diverse enterprise environments, a plus.
  • Familiarity with platforms such as Microsoft Defender, Microsoft Sentinel, CrowdStrike, Tines, Entra ID, and Splunk, a plus.
  • Familiarity with emulation and offensive tooling such as Atomic Red Team, Caldera, Cobalt Strike, or commercial breach and attack simulation platforms, a plus
  • Detection‑as‑code practice: CI/CD pipelines, infrastructure‑as‑code, policy‑as‑code, and automated testing of detection content, a plus.
  • Experience securing or red teaming AI systems, including prompt injection, model evasion, and agent safety testing, a plus
  • Relevant certifications (GCIH, GCFA, GCTI, GPEN, OSCP, Azure Security, or cloud and automation certifications), a plus.

Pay range: $137,000 – 190,600 depending on experience and skill set.
Annual bonus target 10% subject to terms and conditions of plan.
Benefits overview:
ranges may be subject to geographic differentials.

CDW is committed to being an AI-fluent organization

We’re looking for people who bring curiosity, a learner’s mindset, and a willingness to engage with ever-evolving technology and tools. We value adopting AI as a partner, openness to experimentation, and a shared interest in learning together on AI. Our goal is to create a culture where AI enhances—not replaces—human creativity and decision-making. You don’t need to be an expert today; what matters is your readiness to explore, adapt, and grow with us as we integrate AI responsibly and effectively into our work.

Additionally, CDW is committed to fostering an equitable, transparent, and respectful hiring process for all applicants. During our application process, our goal is to understand your experience, strengths, skills, and qualifications. As an AI forward company, we see AI not just as a tool, but as a catalyst for new ways of thinking, creating, and communicating. We encourage candidates to embrace an AI mindset, one that’s curious, adaptive, and ready to explore what’s possible. We welcome thoughtful use of AI to expand your perspective and elevate how you share your story, while ensuring your application remains rooted in your own background, judgment, and voice.

About Us

CDW is a Fortune 500 technology solutions provider that helps businesses, government, education, and healthcare organizations achieve what’s possible through technology. What makes CDW different isn’t just what we do—it’s how we do it. At CDW we act as one—building trust, speaking candidly, and working together to achieve more. We play to win—focusing on what matters most and delivering for our customers. And we think forward—staying curious, moving fast, and continuously learning. We believe meaningful work happens when people feel supported, heard, and empowered to contribute. That’s why we think of ourselves as coworkers, not just employees—working together to solve complex challenges and deliver real impact for our customers and communities.

As a full‑stack, full‑lifecycle technology partner, CDW brings deep expertise, strong relationships, and broad industry knowledge to help turn ideas into outcomes. When you join CDW, you become part of a collaborative environment where your work matters, your growth is supported, and your contributions help shape what’s next.

Together, we deliver the full promise of what technology can do. Together, we Make Amazing Happen.

The Opportunity:

At Avantor, people are the most important part of our success because they drive our global performance. Avantor’s EHS&S vertical is a crucial part of this mix, enabling all our internal teams worldwide to grow beyond their limits.

The Process Safety Manager position is a critical leadership role responsible for the prevention of catastrophic process safety events, management of chemical hazards, regulatory compliance, and implementation of corporate process safety governance across facilities handling hazardous materials. This position supports operational continuity, risk reduction, regulatory compliance, capital projects, emergency preparedness, and protection of employees, communities, assets, and the Avantor brand.

The roles directly support compliance with numerous regulatory frameworks and industry standards, including OSHA Process Safety Management (29 CFR 1910.119), EPA Risk Management Program (40 CFR Part 68), hazardous materials regulations, transportation requirements, fire and building code requirements, occupational safety legislation, and recognized industry best practices established by the Center for Chemical Process Safety (CCPS), American Institute of Chemical Engineers (AIChE), NFPA, and industry insurers. The positions also provide technical oversight for process hazards, Process Hazard Analyses (PHAs), Management of Change (MOC), incident investigations, contractor management, functional safety, and major accident prevention programs.

This position is fully REMOTE.

What we’re looking for:

  • Education: Bachelor's degree in Chemical Engineering, Mechanical Engineering, Environmental Engineering, Occupational Health & Safety, Industrial Engineering, or a closely related technical discipline preferred
  • Certifications (Preferred)
    • Certified Safety Professional (CSP)
    • Certified Process Safety Professional (CCPSC)
    • Professional Engineer (PE)
    • Incident Investigation or Root Cause Analysis certification/training
  • Experience: Minimum of 5-8 years of progressive EHS and/or Process Safety experience within chemical manufacturing, life sciences, specialty chemicals, pharmaceuticals, industrial manufacturing, oil & gas, or related high-hazard industries
    • Demonstrated experience managing OSHA PSM and EPA RMP-covered processes.
    • Experience facilitating Process Hazard Analyses (PHA) and HAZOP studies.
    • Experience leading Management of Change (MOC) programs and incident investigations.
    • Proven ability to partner effectively with operations, engineering, maintenance, and leadership teams.
    • Experience supporting multiple facilities and geographically dispersed operations preferred.
    • Experience working in a corporate or regional process safety role preferred.

Who you are:

  • Expert knowledge of OSHA Process Safety Management (29 CFR 1910.119).
  • Strong knowledge of EPA Risk Management Program (40 CFR Part 68).
  • Understanding of CCPS risk-based process safety principles and methodologies.
  • Knowledge of NFPA standards, hazardous materials management, fire protection systems, and process safety engineering principles.
  • Proficiency in risk assessment tools including HAZOP, What-If Analysis, FMEA, LOPA, Bow-Tie Analysis, and Root Cause Analysis methodologies.
  • Ability to interpret engineering drawings, P&IDs, process flow diagrams, and technical specifications.
  • Strong project management and organizational skills.
  • Exceptional analytical and problem-solving capabilities.
  • Ability to influence stakeholders and drive change without direct authority.
  • Effective written, verbal, and presentation communication skills.
  • Ability to manage multiple priorities across numerous facilities simultaneously.
  • Strong facilitation and leadership skills for cross-functional teams.
  • Proficiency with Microsoft Office Suite and process safety or EHS management systems.
  • Ability to work independently in a remote environment while maintaining high levels of collaboration and engagement.

How you will thrive and create and impact:

Process Safety Program Leadership

  • Lead the development, implementation, deployment, and continuous improvement of the company's Process Safety Management and Risk Management programs.
  • Establish corporate process safety standards, procedures, governance processes, and performance expectations.
  • Ensure process safety programs align with regulatory requirements, industry best practices, and corporate objectives.
  • Act as the primary technical resource for process safety-related matters throughout North America operations.

Regulatory Compliance and Risk Management

  • Ensure compliance with OSHA PSM, EPA RMP, NFPA standards, hazardous materials regulations, and other applicable requirements.
  • Interpret regulatory changes and translate requirements into actionable compliance programs.
  • Conduct compliance assessments and identify opportunities for risk reduction and program enhancement.
  • Support interactions with regulatory agencies, insurance representatives, and third-party auditors.

Process Hazard Analysis (PHA) and Risk Assessment

  • Plan, facilitate, and document Process Hazard Analyses including HAZOP, What-If, Checklist, FMEA, Layer of Protection Analysis (LOPA), and other risk assessment methodologies.
  • Lead multidisciplinary teams in identifying process hazards, evaluating safeguards, and recommending risk reduction measures.
  • Track and verify completion of PHA recommendations and corrective actions.
  • Support facility siting studies, chemical hazard evaluations, and major accident prevention initiatives.

Management of Change (MOC)

  • Lead and maintain formal MOC processes for equipment, technology, procedures, chemicals, and organizational changes.
  • Review proposed modifications to ensure safety, environmental, operational, and regulatory risks are appropriately evaluated and controlled.
  • Verify implementation of required safeguards prior to startup.

Incident Investigation and Root Cause Analysis

  • Lead or support investigations involving process safety incidents, near-misses, releases, fires, explosions, and significant operational events.
  • Utilize recognized root cause analysis methodologies to identify underlying causes and systemic improvements.
  • Ensure corrective actions are developed, implemented, and verified for effectiveness.
  • Share lessons learned across the organization to prevent recurrence.

Mechanical Integrity and Asset Reliability Support

  • Collaborate with Engineering and Maintenance teams to strengthen mechanical integrity programs and inspection strategies.
  • Support risk-based inspection programs and reliability initiatives for critical process equipment.
  • Evaluate deficiencies impacting process safety and recommend corrective actions.
  • Assist in the development of preventive maintenance and inspection requirements.

Capital Projects and New Product Introductions

  • Provide process safety oversight for facility expansions, process modifications, new technologies, and capital projects.
  • Conduct design reviews and hazard assessments during project development and implementation phases.
  • Participate in Pre-Startup Safety Reviews (PSSR) and startup readiness evaluations.
  • Support safe introduction of new products, raw materials, and manufacturing processes.

Auditing, Assessments, and Continuous Improvement

  • Conduct process safety audits, compliance assessments, gap analyses, and site evaluations.
  • Monitor closure of corrective actions resulting from audits, inspections, incident investigations, and insurance recommendations.
  • Develop and track process safety performance indicators (KPIs).
  • Identify opportunities to improve operational effectiveness and risk reduction efforts.

Emergency Preparedness and Business Continuity

  • Support emergency response planning, crisis management, and major incident preparedness activities.
  • Assess facility emergency response capabilities related to hazardous materials and process safety events.
  • Participate in drills, exercises, and emergency response evaluations.
  • Provide technical guidance during safety emergencies when needed.

Training, Coaching, and Organizational Development

  • Develop and deliver process safety training programs for leadership, engineers, operators, maintenance personnel, and EHS professionals.
  • Promote a proactive process safety culture across all operational sites.
  • Mentor facility teams process hazard recognition and risk management practices.
  • Build organizational process safety competency and knowledge sharing programs.

WEB DEVELOPER

Independent Contractor | Remote | Minimum 10 Hours/Week

This is an independent contractor (1099) position. VaVa contractors are responsible for managing their own taxes, benefits, and business expenses.

VaVa Virtual Assistants is a remote company based out of Atlanta, Georgia, built on the belief that businesses thrive when they have the right support behind them. We connect clients across industries like nonprofit, legal, coaching, and finance with skilled virtual professionals who bring genuine expertise to the work. Our team may be distributed, but the culture is deeply connected through daily conversation, project collaboration, and regular all-company virtual gatherings.

We are looking for an experienced Web Developer who is already freelancing or running their own web development practice and wants to supplement that work with additional client projects through VaVa. This role calls for both front end and backend expertise, along with the technical range to move between quick maintenance requests, full site builds, and ecommerce or security work as each project demands.

Beyond your client work, you will be part of a contractor community that genuinely invests in one another's success. Regular calls with clients and fellow contractors keep you connected to the broader VaVa team, and every interaction is an opportunity to reflect our mission, vision, and values.

Please review the requirements and qualifications below carefully, as they reflect what it truly takes to succeed in this role. We appreciate your interest in joining the team.

EXPECTATIONS

Represent VaVa Virtual Assistants in a Positive and Professional Manner

  • Demonstrate strong technical judgment and professionalism in every client interaction.
  • Ensure all communication reflects VaVa's values and standard of quality.
  • Contribute to a collaborative culture among fellow VaVa contractors, including designers or other specialists who may support your projects.

Take Ownership of Client Satisfaction

  • Manage client website projects and ongoing support requests with reliability and follow-through.
  • Anticipate technical needs before they become urgent issues, and communicate proactively about progress and timelines.
  • Deliver work that meets each client's brand, functionality, and performance goals.
  • Adjust availability and scope as project demands shift, from routine maintenance to full site builds or migrations.

RESPONSIBILITIES

  • Design, develop, and maintain websites for multiple clients across a range of industries, primarily using WordPress.

GENERAL QUALIFICATIONS

jobs.excerpt: Group Finance Director – Insurance & InvestmentsAbout the RoleThe Group Finance Director is a senior leadership position responsible for overseeing the Group's financial management, planning, reporting, controls, treasury, and performance across its insurance, investment, asset management, and other financial services businesses.
jobs.description:
Group Finance Director – Insurance & Investments

About the Role

The Group Finance Director is a senior leadership position responsible for overseeing the Group's financial management, planning, reporting, controls, treasury, and performance across its insurance, investment, asset management, and other financial services businesses.

The role provides strategic financial leadership across subsidiaries and business units, ensuring strong financial performance, regulatory compliance, capital discipline, effective risk management, and high-quality decision support for the Group CFO, CEO, Board, and shareholders.

Key Responsibilities

Lead Group-wide financial planning, budgeting, forecasting, and performance management.

Oversee consolidated financial reporting, management accounts, statutory accounts, and financial analysis across subsidiaries.

Drive FP&A, profitability analysis, cost optimization, and financial performance improvement.

Monitor financial performance across insurance, investments, asset management, and other Group businesses.

Oversee insurance finance, including premium revenue, claims, reserves, reinsurance, underwriting performance, and profitability analysis.

Lead financial reporting and accounting oversight for investment and asset management portfolios, including valuation, income, performance, and reporting.

Support Group-level capital planning, solvency, liquidity, and balance-sheet management.

Oversee treasury, cash management, funding requirements, and working-capital optimization.

Strengthen Group-wide financial controls, governance, policies, and risk management frameworks.

Ensure compliance with applicable accounting standards, tax requirements, insurance regulations, investment regulations, and statutory reporting obligations.

Provide financial analysis for M&A, joint ventures, strategic investments, restructuring, and capital allocation decisions.

Partner with senior executives to improve business-unit profitability, operating efficiency, and return on capital.

Lead finance transformation, including ERP, automation, management reporting, analytics, and digital finance initiatives.

Develop and mentor Finance Directors, Controllers, Heads of Finance, and senior finance teams across the Group.

Act as a key financial advisor to the Group CFO, CEO, Executive Committee, Board, auditors, regulators, investors, and other stakeholders.

Key Performance Indicators (KPIs)

Group revenue, EBITDA/profitability, and earnings growth

ROE / ROIC and return on capital

Budget and forecast accuracy

Cost-to-income and expense efficiency

Insurance underwriting and investment profitability

Capital adequacy and solvency position

Liquidity and treasury efficiency

Investment portfolio financial performance

Quality and timeliness of Group reporting

Regulatory and statutory compliance

Strength of internal controls and audit outcomes

Successful finance transformation and process automation

Value creation across subsidiaries and business units

Candidate Profile

15–20+ years of progressive finance experience, preferably within insurance, investment management, asset management, banking, pensions, reinsurance, or diversified financial services.

Proven experience operating at Group / regional / multi-entity level.

Previous experience as Group Finance Director, Finance Director, Group Financial Controller, Deputy Group CFO, Financial Controller, or senior finance executive.

Strong understanding of insurance accounting, investment accounting, financial reporting, capital management, treasury, and regulatory finance.

Demonstrated experience managing complex consolidated reporting structures and multiple subsidiaries.

Strong commercial understanding of investment portfolios, financial markets, capital allocation, and business performance.

Experience supporting M&A, corporate transactions, strategic investments, or restructuring is highly desirable.

Strong leadership experience managing geographically dispersed finance teams.

Education & Professional Qualifications

Bachelor's/Master's degree in Finance, Accounting, Economics, Business, or related discipline.

Professional qualification such as CA, ACCA, CPA, CMA, CFA, or equivalent is strongly preferred.

Additional qualifications in insurance, investment management, or financial risk are advantageous.

Core Competencies

Strategic Finance | Group Consolidation | FP&A | Financial Reporting | Insurance Finance | Investment Finance | Capital Management | Treasury | Solvency | Financial Controls | Regulatory Reporting | M&A | Risk Management | Tax | Finance Transformation | Investor & Board Reporting

Leadership Characteristics

Strategic and commercially minded

Strong analytical and financial judgment

High integrity and governance orientation

Excellent stakeholder and Board communication

Results-driven and performance-focused

Strong people leadership and succession-planning capability

Comfortable operating in complex, regulated, multi-entity environments

Reporting Line

Reports to: Group CFO / Group CEO

Key Stakeholders: Board of Directors, Executive Committee, Group CFO, CEOs/MDs of subsidiaries, Investment & Risk teams, Regulators, Auditors, Investors, and Shareholders.

Target Sourcing Titles

Group Finance Director | Group Financial Director | Group CFO | Deputy Group CFO | Finance Director | Group Financial Controller | Financial Controller | Regional Finance Director | Director of Finance | Head of Group Finance | Head of Finance | VP Finance | Deputy CFO | Finance Executive Director | Group Finance Controller

Position Summary

The Chief API Officer (CAPIO) is responsible for establishing and executing the organization's Application Programming Interface (API) strategy, governance, and ecosystem development initiatives. This executive leads API product management, developer experience, platform integration, Open Banking/Open Finance initiatives, API monetization, security, and digital ecosystem expansion. The role serves as the bridge between business strategy and technology innovation, ensuring APIs become strategic assets that drive revenue, partnerships, customer engagement, and digital transformation.

Key Responsibilities

Strategic Leadership

  • Develop and execute the enterprise-wide API strategy aligned with business objectives.
  • Establish APIs as strategic products and revenue-generating assets.
  • Drive API-first and platform-centric business models across the organization.
  • Identify opportunities for ecosystem expansion through API enablement.
  • Advise executive leadership and the Board on API innovation and digital ecosystem trends.

API Product Management

  • Oversee the API lifecycle from design and development to deployment and retirement.
  • Define API product roadmaps and service portfolios.

  • Drive adoption of API product management best practices.

  • Ensure consistency, scalability, and interoperability across API platforms.

  • Promote API reuse and enterprise integration strategies.

Developer Ecosystem & Partnerships

  • Develop API onboarding programs and developer support initiatives.
  • Foster innovation through open APIs and third-party integrations.
  • Collaborate with external developers, fintechs, vendors, and strategic partners.
  • Lead developer experience (DX) improvements.

API Monetization & Commercial Strategy

  • Develop API monetization models and pricing strategies.
  • Create new revenue streams through API products and services.
  • Identify commercial partnership opportunities leveraging APIs.
  • Monitor API usage, consumption trends, and profitability.
  • Support marketplace and ecosystem expansion strategies.

Open Banking & Open Finance Leadership

  • Lead Open Banking, Open Finance, and Embedded Finance API initiatives.
  • Ensure compliance with industry standards and regulatory requirements.
  • Drive innovation through financial data-sharing ecosystems.
  • Develop strategic API partnerships with financial institutions and fintech organizations.

Security, Risk & Compliance

  • Ensure API security and data protection standards are maintained.
  • Oversee authentication, authorization, and access management frameworks.
  • Implement API cybersecurity best practices.
  • Ensure compliance with privacy regulations, industry standards, and regulatory requirements.
  • Manage operational, security, and third-party risks.

Technology & Innovation

  • Drive adoption of modern API technologies and integration platforms.
  • Oversee API gateways, management platforms, and developer portals.
  • Support cloud-native architectures and microservices transformation.
  • Evaluate emerging technologies including AI, blockchain, and event-driven architectures.
  • Promote continuous innovation and automation.

Data & Analytics

  • Monitor API performance and business outcomes.
  • Establish API analytics and reporting frameworks.
  • Utilize data insights to optimize API products and customer experiences.
  • Measure ecosystem growth and API adoption metrics.

Team Leadership

  • Build and lead high-performing API product, engineering, architecture, and developer relations teams.
  • Foster a culture of innovation, collaboration, and customer-centricity.
  • Develop future leaders and technical experts within the API organization.

Required Qualifications

Education

  • Bachelor's degree in Computer Science, Information Technology, Engineering, Business Administration, or related field.
  • MBA or Master's degree preferred.

Experience

  • 12+ years of leadership experience in API management, enterprise architecture, digital platforms, software engineering, fintech, or technology sectors.
  • Proven experience developing and managing enterprise API ecosystems.
  • Strong background in Open Banking, Open Finance, platform strategies, or digital transformation initiatives.
  • Experience leading large-scale integration and developer ecosystem programs.

Technical Knowledge

  • API Design & Architecture
  • REST, GraphQL, gRPC, and Event-Driven APIs
  • API Gateways & Management Platforms
  • Open Banking & Open Finance Standards
  • Cloud Computing & Microservices
  • Enterprise Integration
  • Cybersecurity & Identity Management
